question: Can the exact derivative through 100 coefficient-recovery steps be computed without treating recovery as an identity or freezing its coefficients?
reuse: First eleven blocks fixed at existing synthetic ProDistill result. Their teachers and weights are unchanged along this direction.
direction: The four current publication tensors minus their original expert values; one prescribed direction, no direction search or defense update.
precision: FP64 shadow of last-block recovery; original FP32 historical results unchanged. Identical duplicated input groups reduced algebraically to 64 student forwards, with the original sum of both teacher losses.
inner: Pinned author coefficient formula, initial .3, Adam lr .01 betas .9/.999 eps1e-8, 100 updates. Public second teacher has zero task vector and hence zero coefficient gradient.
outer_metrics: mean recovered cross entropy against frozen clean expert synthetic predictions
check: Compare analytic forward tangents with pinned author wrapper plus torch.optim.Adam at zero and four numerical perturbations. Primal maximum weight error <1e-8; second central difference agrees within 1e-5 +2% of derivative.
limits: One local direction on historical defender-side synthetic inputs; not a new effective defense, a full gradient, a real-data attack or an equivalence claim to TAR.
stopping: Keep numerical or implementation failure. Fix clear code defects only; no performance-based amplitude, steps, seed, layer or input search.
